h: פּוּרִים, מַאֲמָר ד׳ Purim — Maamar Daled

p: The matter of what they said
that is, the redemption of Egypt
It is that the redemption of Egypt
was the head of all the miracles,
and was the beginning of the revelation
of the holiness of Yisrael in the world;
and the miracle was revealed to the whole world,
that Hashem Yisbarach chose us as a nation
that are outside the way of nature,
However, the miracle of Purim is called
because everything was in great concealment
and she found favor in his eyes,
and the exaltation of the Jews.
And this is what they said (Chullin 139b):
"Where is Esther alluded to in the Torah?
And as is brought in the holy sefarim
that the essential descent of a person
that he is in a state of hester panim;
and this is what it says,
that He will hide the hiding of the Face.
And this was the essence of the miracle of Purim:
that they were then at the lowest level,
that they stood in utter concealment,
and fasting, and weeping, and lamenting," etc.
And as is known, mourning and eulogy
that has been settled in a person's mind
that his hope is already lost,
like mourning and eulogy for the dead,
whom there is no way to bring back;
and through this that they felt
it was transformed for them from mourning to a festival.
And this is what they said (Megillah 11a):
"When did all the ends of the earth see
In the days of Mordechai and Esther."
The intent of what it says,
"all the ends of the earth saw,"
is not the nations of the world,
close to the way of nature, as mentioned above.
"And many of the peoples of the land became Jews,"
was only out of fear of the Jews
for they saw that the king had elevated him
for the sake of the honor of Queen Esther.
"all the ends of the earth saw"
who were then in utter lowliness,
in the concealment, down to the ends of the earth;
they saw the salvation of our God,
And this matter sparkles forth every year
it becomes known to every individual Jewish soul:
whoever knows the afflictions of his heart,
how he is at the lowest level,
and he is embittered over this,
through this itself it becomes known and shines in his heart
that it has been transformed for him from sorrow to joy.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Nasso 12 — “The main error is that the aspect of concealment is hidden from a person, and it seems to him that nothing is hidden from his mind.” Rav Tzadok reads the same doubled “haster astir” there as concealment of the concealment, and draws the remedy that matches this maamar: safety begins once a person knows that something is hidden from him.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Keter Shem Tov I, §55 — “'I shall surely hide My face' means that He hides so that they will not know that the Holy One, blessed be He, is present there in concealment. ... Once a person knows this great principle—that no barrier separates him from his God during Torah and prayer—even if many alien thoughts arise, these are garments and coverings in which God is concealed. Once the person knows that God is concealed there, it is no longer concealment.” This is an exact earlier formulation of the twofold concealment invoked here under 'the holy books.'

paragraphs.text: Connection: The earlier teaching distinguishes concealment from unawareness of concealment. Rav Tzadok applies the same distinction to Purim and to the individual: recognizing one's low condition already allows the hidden Divine rescue to be perceived.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Sod Yesharim, Purim 22 — “When Hashem saves, He illuminates even the concealment that came before, showing that in the time of hiddenness there was also light.” The Radziner adds that the salvation does not only end the concealment but lights it up after the fact, which is how the salvation could be seen precisely from within it.
